title: AI Hallucinations in State Farm Insurance Outside Lawyers' Filings

reading.body:
This is a case of a model asserting fabricated information as fact inside a formal legal process. An attorney used an AI legal drafting tool called Irys to help prepare court filings, and the tool generated case citations, case titles, and quoted holdings that do not exist. Seven nonexistent citations appeared across eight separate filings before the error was discovered. The failure occurred at the drafting stage, before any human verification of the cited sources.

The failure mode is AI hallucination deployed without an adequate review step. The attorney believed the tool performed accuracy checks through an integrated legal research subscription, but that belief was mistaken. A manual check of each citation against an authoritative legal database would have caught the fabrications before filing. No such check was performed.

It is not established that State Farm itself directed the use of the AI tool or had prior knowledge of the citations' inaccuracy. The admissions reported are those of outside counsel, and the case had not concluded at the time of reporting, so no court findings or sanctions are yet on record.

reports.title: State Farm defense lawyers admit AI generated fake cases in LA lawsuit
AI hallucinated case law in insurance company’s filings in L.A. County house fire dispute
AI Hallucinations in State Farm Insurance Outside Lawyers' Filings

summary:
# Summary

Lawyers representing State Farm in a Los Angeles lawsuit involving a home damaged by fire have apologized for submitting court documents containing artificial intelligence-generated fake cases, false quotes, and nonexistent legal holdings. The homeowner, Fa'alagilagi Meni-Siliga, filed suit in July 2024 after a 2020 fire in her Carson home made it uninhabitable. Following contractor repairs and storm damage, State Farm allegedly delayed approving additional work, leaving the home unfinished. Meni-Siliga and her husband exhausted their savings, declared bankruptcy, and lost their home to foreclosure. The case proceeds to trial in October 2025.

State Farm lawyer Jacquelene Robinson admitted using an AI tool called Irys to help prepare filings, incorrectly believing it performed accuracy checks through her firm's legal research subscription. She confirmed seven case citations across eight filings did not exist, along with incorrect case titles and fabricated quotes. Lead counsel Kenneth Katel accepted responsibility for the errors and stated the firm updated its AI policy. State Farm said it expects external counsel to maintain the highest ethical standards. This incident reflects broader concerns as 41 percent of law firms now use generative AI, with a Paris-based researcher documenting nearly 1,900 legal hallucination cases worldwide.
